statement: enforcer-lang-cfml (e-pack-cfml) stood up the CFML/ColdFusion Validator crate from scratch: 20 fixture-provable T1/T2 validators across rules::arch (layered architecture, WireBox DI), rules::security (SQLi/XSS/secrets/info-disclosure), rules::style (var scoping, typed signatures, banned evaluate/iif, naming/access/logging/dead-code), rules::err (typed throw, no swallowed catch), and rules::toolchain (box.json/.cflintrc/CI/TestBox manifest checks) — plus a separate rules::cflint_adapter (CFML-CPLX-2.1) that shells out to the real cflint binary as an advisory-only signal. All 20 fixture-provable validators + registry-smoke + rule_registry tests are green; cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-cfml -D warnings is clean; cargo build --workspace is clean.
why: CFML was a total greenfield gap — no crate, no coldfusion language key, no .cfc/.cfm fixtures existed before this pack, and the enforcer has no CFML AST/parser (unlike syn for Rust or tree-sitter for TS/Dart), so every rule here had to be a line/keyword text detector mirroring enforcer-lang-common's rules::fsm/rules::size_shape shape.
howToApply: Future CFML rule additions should follow this crate's module split (arch/security/style/err/toolchain) and reuse rules::support's finding()/first_line_containing helpers rather than re-deriving them. The FSM (CF-FSM-*) and size/complexity (CF-SIZE-*) rows from the workpack are deliberately NOT re-implemented here — they compose with enforcer-lang-common's existing FSM-*/SIZE-* validators (d16/d22); this crate only needed to supply CFML appliesTo + fixtures for those, which was out of this session's L32 research budget and is left as a follow-up (see mem-e-pack-cfml-0003).

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-lang-cfml: 11 passed (6 unit + 2 fixture_parity + 3 rule_registry); cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-cfml -- -D warnings: clean

statement: The CFLint shell-out adapter (rules::cflint_adapter::CflintAdvisoryValidator) is deliberately EXCLUDED from enforcer_lang_cfml::all_validators() (the vec the uniform tests/fixture_parity.rs harness proves) because its output legitimately differs by host: an honest Severity::Info 'tool unavailable, check skipped' finding when cflint is absent from PATH vs. a real Warning-severity advisory finding when it runs. run_fixture_parity's contract (pass fixture => exactly zero findings) cannot hold for a validator that ALWAYS emits something on one branch or the other, so it is proven instead by dedicated unit tests in rules::cflint_adapter::tests: parse_cflint_report round-trip, a pure map_report_to_findings() mapping test (bypasses the actual subprocess), and a test that asserts Severity::Info + a 'skipped' title when the binary is genuinely unavailable.
why: A naive design would have made the CFLint adapter's validate() always return a Vec<Finding> including the skip case, then tried to run it through the same fixture-parity loop as every other validator — that breaks on any CI runner that does or doesn't have cflint installed, non-deterministically. Splitting 'the honest-skip/report-mapping contract' out of the uniform harness is the correct fix, not a workaround, because the graceful-skip diagnostic is not the same kind of thing as a structural rule violation.
howToApply: Any future arc-18-style external-tool shell-out validator (CommandBox, cfformat, TestBox coverage) should follow the same split: keep it OUT of the crate's all_validators() that feeds run_fixture_parity, and prove its graceful-skip + report-mapping behavior with dedicated unit tests that do not depend on the external binary being present on the test-runner's PATH.

statement: enforcer-rules::RuleRecord (arc-04's actual Rust schema) has no appliesTo/language field — it only carries ruleId/version/title/tier/validator/fixtures/docAnchor/tags. The e-pack-cfml workpack's acceptance text (written against the legacy .mjs-era vocabulary) asks for a test proving 'coldfusion/.cfc/.cfm registered as rule records', which this pack satisfied via crates/enforcer-lang-cfml/tests/rule_registry.rs asserting every record carries a 'coldfusion' tag plus .cfc/.cfm fixture extensions (exempting the box.json/.cflintrc/CI-manifest-scoped toolchain rules) — the closest honest proxy the current schema supports. The CF-FSM-*/CF-SIZE-* rows (workpack items pointing at d16/d22) were NOT added as separate rule records in this pass; they were left out because d16/d22 already own FSM-*/SIZE-* rule ids in enforcer-lang-common and this pack's L32 budget did not cover writing CFML-specific appliesTo/fixtures for those existing ids without risking scope creep into enforcer-lang-common's territory.
why: Any future pass tightening arc-04's RuleRecord schema to add a first-class appliesTo/language field should re-visit every lang-* crate's registry test (this one included) since they are all currently proving language coverage indirectly via tags/fixture-extensions, not a typed field.
howToApply: A follow-up task (out of this pack's exact-file-claims scope) should: (1) decide whether enforcer-rules::RuleRecord should gain a typed appliesTo/language field, and if so migrate every lang-*.json catalog at once; (2) add CFML fixtures for enforcer-lang-common's FSM-*/SIZE-* families (CF-FSM-1.1..2.5, CF-SIZE-FILE/FUNC/CLASS/PARAMS/LINE-1.1) the same way this pack added .cfc/.cfm fixtures for its own T1/T2 rows, without touching enforcer-lang-common's Rust source.
